<!--
Read CONTRIBUTING.md first. Contributions are not solicited by default, and an idea
opened here is read with interest but carries no commitment that it will be built.
Repositories that accept contributions say so themselves.

If you want to know whether something is worth your time to implement, ask here
BEFORE writing the code rather than after.
-->

## Repository

Which repository this concerns, or "new" if it does not fit an existing one.

## What you are trying to do

The problem, not the solution. What are you actually after?

## What you have in mind

Your proposed direction, if you have one.

## What you have already considered

Alternatives you weighed, and why you set them aside. Optional, but it is usually the
most useful part of a proposal.

## Would you want to implement it yourself?

Say so if you would. It changes the answer — see CONTRIBUTING.md for the conventions
that apply if a repository does accept the work: signed commits, sign-off, and one
subject per pull request.
